newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FOREST'S BID FOR WADDLE RUNS INTO TROUBLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FOREST'S BID FOR WADDLE RUNS INTO TROUBLE.

text.p: Nottingham Forest's bid to sign former England winger Chris Waddle appeared to have run aground on Thursday when his current club Bradford threatened to block the move.
Waddle said earlier in the day he expected to agree a deal with the premier league side within hours while Forest said they were confident of signing him before the weekend.
But first division Bradford have threatened to report Forest to the Football Association for illegally approaching the 36-year-old winger while he was still under contract.
They say there is no clause in Waddle's contract allowing him to leave, even though he joined them on a free transfer.
"It all boils down to a verbal agreement I had with the club and obviously because it's not in writing someone along the line is contesting it," Waddle said.
"I left last night thinking I was going to join Forest but obviously there's some problem...I don't know what the problem is."
Waddle made his name with Newcastle, Tottenham and former European champions Marseille. Although past his prime, he is still one of the most creative players in the English game.
"Everybody knows about Chris's ability and he would be a wonderful asset to us," Forest general manager Dave Bassett said.
If Waddle does sign, he will become the third forward to join Forest in a matter of days.

On Monday they signed Dutch striker Pierre Van Hooydonk from Glasgow Celtic for an initial fee of 3.0 million pounds ($4.8 million) and on Thursday they confirmed the signing of England under-21 striker Ian Moore from first division Tranmere.
Forest were the subject of a successful takeover bid last month which freed up around 16 million pounds ($25.6 million) for new players.
They are 18th in the 20-team premier league and have scored just two goals in their last eight matches.
